heard: A black hole replacing our Sun would not sucker thin. Hollywood often portrays these compact objects as cosmic vacuum cleaners devouring everything in their surroundings. However, Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass. Because the pull depends only on mass, replacing the Sun with an identical mass black hole changes nothing. The solar material would simply compress into an event-horizon boundary, only three kilometers wide. To get trapped, an object must cross this shore-scaled radius where even light cannot escape. Outside that boundary, infalling matter actually heats up and emits x-rays before crossing the point of no return. But at our distant orbit, Earth would safely circle the dark remnant forever.

'schwarzschild' heard as 'shore scaled' after 'must cross this'
